text:
oliver: Quick question for the group — we're planning to improve log<>trace linking across hosted/dedicated/private. Two implementation options: (A) inject trace_id at the app logging layer (lib-level) or (B) enrich logs at ingestion (log-bridge). What are the tradeoffs and a clean migration plan?

sasha: +1 on doing it at the app level where possible. Gives downstream consumers immediate structured fields, simpler for offline analysis. But we need uniform SDKs across languages and a compatibility shim for older services.

devin: We can use OTEL SpanContext to populate structured logs. Example (python + structlog):
```python
from opentelemetry.trace import get_current_span
span = get_current_span()
trace_id = span.get_span_context().trace_id
logger.info("event", trace_id=f"{trace_id:032x}")
```
Same idea in go/java — expose a small helper so apps don't copy/paste.

harper: Important security/privacy note: private/on-prem customers may want to keep enrichment internal. Any plan must allow local-only enrichment and ensure nothing gets out by default. Also watch cardinality: adding free-form IDs to log indices can bloat storage if we create indexes on them.

lina: From product/console POV — we want "open in logs" from a trace view when trace_id is present. UX should fall back to a join by trace_id at ingestion time if app didn't inject it. So ingestion-side enrichment remains necessary as a fallback.

matt: Field naming bikeshed: propose we standardize on snake_case "trace_id" as the canonical log field across all services. Avoid vendor prefixes. Also define length/hex format (32-char lowercase hex).

sasha: Agreed on trace_id, and we should publish a short eng-platform contract doc + a linter rule that flags unknown variants (traceId, trace-id, otel.trace_id).

engops-bot: Deploy queued: log-bridge v2 (#412) — will contain enrichment fallback and new schema mappings.

harper: Retention question: do we plan to store trace_id as a searchable field? If we index trace_id across massive logs that could increase index size. Maybe index with doc-values but not full-text, and limit retention on the indices that contain trace_id to a shorter window.

devin: Also, note that sampled=false spans still carry a trace_id/span_id. We should propagate even when tracers drop spans so logs can link to traces when available. Logging libs should not rely on sampler decision.

oliver: Draft migration plan: 1) Add helper libs (go/java/python) to set trace_id on structured logs (v1). 2) Add linter + field contract enforcement. 3) Deploy app libs and opt-in via a feature flag for canary services. 4) Deploy ingestion-side enrichment as fallback for services we can't upgrade. 5) Console: add "Jump to logs (trace_id)" and QA. 6) Signal to customers (dedicated/private) and provide opt-out. Anything missing?

sasha: Add telemetry: instrument the rollout itself. Count percentage of logs with trace_id per service + control chart so we can detect regressions. Also add a migration playbook for rollback if indexing costs spike.

lina: We'll need a release note and a short template for customer comms. Also include steps for private deployments to run enrichment locally.

matt: I'll take the field contract doc and draft the linter rules. Will propose the snake_case + hex format and a small regex.

harper: I'll prototype index settings for trace_id indices (doc_values:true, disabled norms, short retention). Will simulate storage impact with 30 services.

devin: I'll start the helper libs and a test harness that emits logs with/without trace_id and verifies console linking.

oliver: Perfect. After docs + libs, we'll schedule a 2-week canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

matt: ack

sasha: ack

(ends)
